title: Quasi-coherator for locally quasi-coherent flat-compatible stack modules
statement: Work in the universes and small-site convention of [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $\mathcal Z/S$ an algebraic stack [def-sfb-algebraic-moduli-stack], with big fppf site and structure sheaf as in [def-sfb-stack-quasi-coherent-algebra]. Use module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Write $\operatorname{QCoh}(\mathcal Z)$ for the full category of modules locally admitting a presentation by small direct sums of $\mathcal O_{\mathcal Z}$. For a big-fppf module $H$ and an object $z:T\to\mathcal Z$, let $H_z$ be its restriction to the small etale site $T_{\mathrm{et}}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-site]. Say $H$ is locally quasi-coherent if each $H_z$ is the etale sheaf associated to a quasi-coherent Zariski module $H_z^{\mathrm{Zar}}$ [pqf-def-coherent], with value $\Gamma(V,v^*H_z^{\mathrm{Zar}})$ on an etale map $v:V\to T$. For an arrow $a:z'\to z$ over $u:T'\to T$, restriction induces the tensor comparison $c_a:u^*H_z\to H_{z'}$, where tensor pullback is [def-pc-module-pullback]. Say $H$ is flat-compatible if $c_a$ is an isomorphism whenever $u$ is flat [def-weil-flat-morphism]. Let $\mathcal L_{\mathcal Z}$ be the full subcategory of such locally quasi-coherent flat-compatible modules. The inclusion $j_{\mathcal Z}:\operatorname{QCoh}(\mathcal Z)\hookrightarrow\mathcal L_{\mathcal Z}$ is defined and has a right adjoint $Q_{\mathcal Z}:\mathcal L_{\mathcal Z}\to\operatorname{QCoh}(\mathcal Z)$. Its counit is a natural module map $q_H:j_{\mathcal Z}Q_{\mathcal Z}H\to H$, and composition with $q_H$ gives natural bijections $$\operatorname{Hom}_{\operatorname{QCoh}(\mathcal Z)}(G,Q_{\mathcal Z}H)\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal L_{\mathcal Z}}(j_{\mathcal Z}G,H),\qquad a\longmapsto q_H\circ j_{\mathcal Z}(a).$$ The adjunction unit gives $Q_{\mathcal Z}j_{\mathcal Z}\cong\mathrm{id}$. No quasi-compactness, quasi-separatedness, finiteness or Noetherian hypothesis on $\mathcal Z$ is imposed.

proof.text: For $G\in\operatorname{QCoh}(\mathcal Z)$, the scheme-test restriction criterion gives quasi-coherent $G_z^{\mathrm{Zar}}$ and isomorphisms $u^*G_z\simeq G_{z^\prime}$ for every arrow, naturally and compatibly with composition. Thus $G$ is locally quasi-coherent and flat-compatible; the full inclusion $j$ is defined.

Choose a smooth surjective scheme atlas $f:U\to\mathcal Z$. The chartwise calculus makes it flat and locally finitely presented. The presentation theorem gives $R=U\times_{\mathcal Z}U$ an algebraic-space groupoid with flat locally finitely presented source and target, and an equivalence $[U/R]\simeq\mathcal Z$. The module-descent theorem gives an equivalence $E:\operatorname{QCoh}(\mathcal Z)\simeq\operatorname{QCoh}(U,R)$ whose underlying module is restriction to $U_{\mathrm{et}}$. Fix a quasi-inverse $D$ and its natural isomorphisms.

For $H\in\mathcal L_{\mathcal Z}$ put $M=H_f$. On $R$ write $c_s:s^*M\xrightarrow{\sim}H_{fs}$ and $c_t:t^*M\xrightarrow{\sim}H_{ft}$, and let $b:H_{ft}\xrightarrow{\sim}H_{fs}$ come from the universal two-isomorphism. These are isomorphisms by the algebraic-space comparison calculus and flatness of $s,t$. Define $\alpha_H=c_s^{-1}bc_t:t^*M\to s^*M$. Here $M$ is quasi-coherent. On a triple of atlas points use the notation $c_i:p_i^*M\to H_{f p_i}$ and $b_{ij}:H_{f p_j}\to H_{f p_i}$. Every $p_i$ is flat, and comparison composition identifies the pullback of $\alpha_H$ to the $(i,j)$ relation with $c_i^{-1}b_{ij}c_j$. The groupoid identity gives $b_{12}b_{23}=b_{13}$, so the product is $c_1^{-1}b_{12}c_2c_2^{-1}b_{23}c_3=c_1^{-1}b_{13}c_3$. This is precisely the cocycle equation; on the identity relation $b=1$ and the two comparisons agree, giving $e^*\alpha_H=1$. Thus $(M,\alpha_H)$ is a groupoid module. Naturality of comparisons gives $s^*v\,\alpha_H=\alpha_{H^\prime}t^*v$ for restriction of every $H\to H^\prime$, so this defines a functor $B:\mathcal L_{\mathcal Z}\to\operatorname{QCoh}(U,R)$.

Define $Q=DB$. For $G\in\operatorname{QCoh}(\mathcal Z)$ the equivalence $E$ and its counit identify $\operatorname{Hom}(G,QH)$ with $\operatorname{Hom}(EG,BH)$. The maps-from-quasi-coherent theorem applies because $s,t$ are flat and locally finitely presented and $H$ is a big-fppf module. In its comparison square all four comparisons are invertible, for $G$ by the scheme-test criterion and for $H$ by the comparison calculus. Cancelling them shows that its image condition is exactly $s^*v\,\alpha_G=\alpha_Ht^*v$. Hence restriction identifies $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal L}(jG,H)$ with $\operatorname{Hom}(EG,BH)$. Compose these two bijections to obtain a bijection $\Phi_{G,H}:\operatorname{Hom}(G,QH)\simeq\operatorname{Hom}(jG,H)$. Both equivalence transport and restriction commute with pre- and postcomposition, so $\Phi$ is natural in both arguments. This is $j\dashv Q$.

Set $q_H=\Phi_{QH,H}(1_{QH})$. Naturality in $G$ gives $\Phi_{G,H}(a)=q_H\circ j(a)$, and naturality in $H$ makes $q:jQ\to\mathrm{id}$ a natural module map. To check the unit $\eta_G:G\to QjG$ is invertible, fullness of $j$ gives $r:QjG\to G$ with $j(r)=q_{jG}$. The triangle identity gives $r\eta_G=1_G$ by faithfulness. Also $\Phi_{QjG,jG}(\eta_G r)=q_{jG}j(\eta_G)j(r)=q_{jG}=\Phi_{QjG,jG}(1)$, so injectivity of $\Phi$ gives $\eta_G r=1$. This proves $Qj\cong\mathrm{id}$ with the requested unit. The atlas was arbitrary; no quasi-compactness, quasi-separatedness, finiteness or Noetherian assumption was used.

theorem exists_moduliLqcCoherator {S : Scheme.{u}}
    (F : BasedCategory.{v, w} (Over S)) (hF : IsAlgebraicModuliStack F) :
    ∃ h : SheafOfModules.isQuasicoherent (moduliModuleRings F hF.1.1) ≤
        locallyQuasicoherentFlatCompatible F hF.1.1,
      ∃ Q : (locallyQuasicoherentFlatCompatible F hF.1.1).FullSubcategory ⥤
          (SheafOfModules.isQuasicoherent (moduliModuleRings F hF.1.1)).FullSubcategory,
        ∃ adj : ObjectProperty.ιOfLE h ⊣ Q,
          (∀ (G : (SheafOfModules.isQuasicoherent
                (moduliModuleRings F hF.1.1)).FullSubcategory)
              (H : (locallyQuasicoherentFlatCompatible F hF.1.1).FullSubcategory)
              (a : G ⟶ Q.obj H),
            (adj.homEquiv G H).symm a =
              (ObjectProperty.ιOfLE h).map a ≫ adj.counit.app H) ∧
          IsIso adj.unit
